greeting.title: Hello
greeting.text: Hello! I am Maya. Let us keep Panjim dry.

opening.title: First job
opening.text: Hello! I am Maya. Before the {storm}, our first job is to {objective}. The steps are in the Get ready card, bottom right.

tutorial.start: A cyclone comes in 3 years, and each build is one year. Click a tile on the beach to see what you can build there.
tutorial.cards: Each card says how many homes it protects here from this cyclone. Pick the biggest number.
tutorial.outline: The faint outline shows the homes still at risk. Build inside it to bring them to safety.
tutorial.heat: Red marks the homes this cyclone would flood. This is your last build before it lands.

tips.title: The red warning
tips.text: See the red? That is where the next storm will hit hardest. It shows in the two years before the storm comes.

tips.title: Mangroves
tips.text: Mangroves slow the surge before it reaches the houses. Plant them on the wetland edge.

tips.title: Khazans
tips.text: A khazan holds floodwater, so nearby homes stay drier.

tips.title: Dunes and pandanus
tips.text: Dunes and pandanus shield the beach from a cyclone's surge.

tips.title: Seawalls
tips.text: A seawall holds no water. If a storm is bigger than the wall, it fails all at once.

tips.title: Get ready
tips.text: I keep a short Get ready list for the next storm, bottom right. Every item is optional.

warning.exposed: The red shows where the {storm} will hit. {place} is most at risk: strengthen it now.
warning.lastCall: Last call! {count} homes are still in danger, most of them around {place}.

aftermath.allSaved: Every home in the storm's path is still standing. Panjim is proud of you!
aftermath.someLost: We lost {lost} homes at {place}. A few more defences there next time and they will stand.
aftermath.noDefence: Nothing stood between the {hazard} and {place}. Next time, plant something there first.
aftermath.saved: Without your {defence}, {count} more homes would have been hit.
aftermath.notYet: The {hazard} reached {place} before the defences there could make a difference. More of them there will hold it.

results._comment: Section 9: her one line on the result cards. 'byDefence' names the kind of defence that saved the most homes (a game rule about what it does here, waves and water only: the game does not model wind). 'comingUp' is about the next storm.

dune.text: Dunes took the first push of the waves and held the water back from the homes behind them.

sandy_vegetation.text: Pandanus and creepers bind the sand, so the water loses strength crossing the beach.

seawall.text: The seawall held the water back. A storm too big for it breaks through all at once.

breakwater.text: Breakwaters broke the waves out at sea, before they reached the beach.

mangrove.text: Mangroves slowed the water through their roots and sheltered the streets behind them.

khazan.text: Khazans held the floodwater in their fields, so the homes nearby stayed drier.

small_dam.text: The dam held back the river's rise upstream, so less water reached the wetlands.

flood.text: The flood comes down the Mandovi, through the creek at Ribandar and into Merces, St Cruz and Taleigao. Look at where the map turns red.

compound.text: Next time the waves and the river come together. The beach and the wetlands both need you.
